subject: Hosting and private connectivity confirmation for Yonder pilot
messages:
From: Tom Kiernan <tom.kiernan@yonderhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting and private connectivity confirmation for Yonder pilot

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the pilot looks promising. Before we pull together the SOW and procurement paperwork, our security team needs a short confirmation of a few hosting and private connectivity controls so we can complete the SIG/CAIQ:

1)Can you confirm you can host our instance entirely in an EU region (eu-west-1) including model serving, logs, and control plane data?
2)Do you offer a private connectivity option (VPC peering / PrivateLink / Private endpoint) so traffic between our VPC and Redwood does not traverse the public internet?
3)Can keys be customer-managed (BYOK) in an EU KMS partition, and will Redwood confirm no key material leaves the region?
4)Are there audit logs showing per-request routing/egress, and can you provide a sample runbook or diagram for the private deployment?

Wed appreciate a short packet with diagrams and any SLA/backstop language regarding cross-region fallback. Goal is to close security review early next week.

Attaching the SIG template to this email for your reference.

Thanks,
Tom Kiernan
Security Lead, Yonder Health
Tom.Kiernan@yonderhealth.com

Attachment: Yonder-SIG.xlsx (stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Tom Kiernan <tom.kiernan@yonderhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting and private connectivity confirmation for Yonder pilot

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary answers up front, followed by attachments and a short runbook link.

Summary answers:
- EU-only hosting: Yes. We can provision a dedicated tenant in eu-west-1 for the pilot. Model serving, token logs, and control-plane metadata can be constrained to that region when you choose the Private deployment option.
- Private connectivity: Yes. We support PrivateLink and VPC Peering for Dedicated/Dedicated-Private modes. Private control-plane option is available for enterprise pilots.
- KMS / BYOK: Yes. We support customer-managed keys (BYOK). Keys can be provisioned in your EU KMS and used for token encryption at rest; Redwood never retains raw key material.
- Audit logs & runbook: We provide per-request routing logs, per-token latency/cost metrics, and an operations runbook for failover/fallback.

Attached: redwood-region-deployment-overview.pdf (diagram + stubs) and eu-kms-partitioning-notes.txt (technical notes). Also: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-private-deploy (internal runbook link; I'll paste a sanitized copy into the SIG workbook if helpful).

Next steps I propose:
1)Well fill the SIG workbook (Tom, I can return a baseline completed copy tomorrow).
2)Rishi will supply a short residency evidence spreadsheet and network snippet examples for procurement.
3)If you need contractual language around cross-region fallback, we can surface a proposed clause; generally we recommend an agreed fallback policy with a defined SLA and notification window.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call with Rishi and Kimberly to walk through the diagrams.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-region-deployment-overview.pdf (diagram stub); eu-kms-partitioning-notes.txt (attachment stub)

Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosting and private connectivity confirmation for Yonder pilot

Looping in a couple of technical notes that answer the more granular items Tom listed.

Key points: 
- Residency: For Private deployments the entire control plane can be deployed into your AWS account (private control plane) or into a Redwood-managed tenant that we lock to eu-west-1. In both models, tokens and logs remain within the region. Well provide an audited map showing where artifacts are stored.
- KMS/BYOK: We support BYOK via KMS key policies. The flow is: customer KMS encrypts keys; Redwood gets access via IAM roles to call KMS Encrypt/Decrypt; raw key material is never exported to Redwood. We can provide an example key policy.
- Network: We support PrivateLink, VPC Peering, and Customer-Managed Transit. We can provide a sample terraform snippet for the VPC endpoint and iptables-level egress lock-down (see attached network-configuration-snippets.txt).
- Auditing: We emit per-request audit records to an S3 bucket in your account or to a log-collector in the same region. Those logs include routing decisions and egress metadata.

Attachments: residency-evidence-summary.xlsx (contains per-artifact region map and timestamps), network-configuration-snippets.txt (terraform and export policy examples).

Naomi — Ive added a short paragraph you can paste into the SIG/CAIQ under Data Residency + Network Controls. If Toms team wants, we can also generate a one-page attestation on letterhead.

Rishi
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

Hi Naomi / team,

Appreciate the quick responses and the packet. A couple of final clarifications before we move the SIG to procurement: 

- For BYOK, can you confirm we will be able to provide specific key IDs and see HSM-backed key usage in your audit logs (timestamped, key-id referenced)? We need evidence that key operations are constrained to eu-west-1 and that no backup copies are stored outside the region.
- If there is a cross-region fallback (for example an incident requiring failover to us-west), can we get proposed contract language that limits fallback to read-only operations and requires 24-hour notice and approval from Yonder security?
- Can you attach the SOC2 mapping or direct us to the SOC2 report that mentions region controls and network isolation?

If those items look good, procurement will draft the SOW and well move forward.

Ive attached our completed SIG workbook with a few highlighted items (Yonder-SIG.xlsx). Procurement is ccd on this thread.

Best,
Tom
Security Lead, Yonder Health

Attachment: Yonder-SIG.xlsx (updated stub)
